title: Donald Trump announces presidential exploratory committee
description_short: Donald Trump announces presidential exploratory committee
description_medium: On March 18, 2015, Donald Trump announced that he had formed a presidential exploratory committee, moving toward a possible 2016 campaign before deciding whether to enter the race formally. The announcement followed reports that he had hired political operatives earlier that year and included criticism of the country’s direction.
description_long: On March 18, 2015, Donald Trump announced the formation of a presidential exploratory committee, a step toward a possible run in the 2016 election. Reports that he had hired political operatives in February, including people previously associated with the Koch network, had made a campaign announcement less surprising. Trump used the announcement to argue that the country was in serious trouble and had lost respect internationally. An exploratory committee signaled organized consideration of a campaign while leaving a formal candidacy announcement for a later step. The supplied excerpt cuts off during Trump’s remarks, so it does not preserve the complete speech or establish the committee’s initial staffing, fundraising, or operations. The event marked a shift from public speculation about another presidential bid to an organized public step toward one.
notes: The supplied synopsis supports the announcement, timing, prior hiring of operatives and a partial statement; it does not provide the complete speech or initial committee operations.

title: Trump Inappropriately Profited Since Returning to Power, Say 69% of Americans
description_short: Trump Inappropriately Profited Since Returning to Power, Say 69% of Americans
description_medium: A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found that 69% of Americans believe Trump has inappropriately profited since returning to power. This perception is likely due to various reports of Trump's financial dealings and potential conflicts of interest. The poll suggests that a significant majority of Americans are concerned about Trump's financial activities and their potential impact on his decision-making.
description_long: The linked Reuters report describes a four-day Reuters/Ipsos poll completed on Monday and reports two separate findings. It says 69% of respondents thought Trump’s private business interests influenced his presidential decisions; separately, 63% said it was inappropriate for Trump and his family to profit from cryptocurrency ventures. The article also reports that about half of Republicans thought business interests influenced his decisions, while the White House denied conflicts and Trump said he had no day-to-day role in the family business. These are respondents’ judgments, not a legal finding that Trump committed wrongdoing. The supplied title and preserved medium collapse the influence and profit questions into one claim, so they should not be treated as the wording or result of a single poll question. The available excerpt does not give the sample size or exact question text.

title: Trump Sued Over Selling Early Access to Truth Social Posts
description_short: Trump Sued Over Selling Early Access to Truth Social Posts
description_medium: A federal lawsuit has been filed against President Donald Trump, accusing him of violating the First Amendment by selling special advance access to his Truth Social posts. The lawsuit claims that this practice is unconstitutional and gives certain individuals unfair access to the president's thoughts and ideas.
description_long: A federal lawsuit filed in the Southern District of New York on August 12, 2026, accused the Trump administration of violating the First Amendment by selling advance access to Truth Social posts. The plaintiffs were the Freedom of the Press Foundation and The Intercept, represented by several legal organizations. Their complaint challenged Truth API, a service announced by Truth Social’s parent company that offered early access to posts by Trump and other officials for as much as $100,000 per month; the report said at least 10 customers had signed up. The plaintiffs argued that the president was monetizing public statements and providing market-moving government information to paying users. The report noted that Trump held a 41% stake in Trump Media & Technology Group through a trust controlled by one of his sons, and that the administration had treated his Truth Social posts as official presidential statements in other contexts. These are allegations in a newly filed case, not a court ruling. The White House had not responded to the request for comment when the report was published.
notes: The linked ABC News mirror provided the filing date and court, plaintiffs, challenged service, reported pricing and customers, ownership disclosure, and the complaint’s First Amendment theory. The allegations had not been adjudicated in the report.

title: Trump Insiders Warn of Tsunami Hitting West Wing
description_short: Trump insiders have warned of a 'tsunami' barreling at the West Wing. The warning comes as the Trump administration faces various challenges and controversies.
description_medium: A Daily Mail report published August 21, 2026, quoted unnamed Trump allies warning that the White House was unprepared for possible congressional investigations if Democrats won control of either chamber in the fall. The article listed several subjects they expected to face scrutiny and tied the warning to planned changes in White House legal staff.
description_long: A Daily Mail report published August 21, 2026, said people close to Trump feared the White House was not ready for congressional investigations if Democrats won the House or Senate in the November midterms. The article quoted an unnamed source predicting a “tsunami” of Democratic lawyers and listed possible subjects of scrutiny: the Trump family’s cryptocurrency business, Washington renovations and a planned ballroom, stock trades, immigration enforcement, the new Air Force One, and the release of Epstein files. The report connected the warning to a change in the White House counsel’s office. Will Scharf was expected to replace David Warrington on September 1, while associate counsel Samuel Adkisson was leaving after Trump nominated him for a federal judgeship. Other sources said the office needed to add staff; the report also described disagreement among Trump allies about Scharf’s legal advice on the Insurrection Act and habeas corpus. The predicted investigations were contingent on election results, not actions that had already occurred.
notes: The linked report identifies the conditional warning, issues named by sources, and expected counsel-office changes. The “tsunami” language is an attributed forecast, not evidence that those investigations occurred.
